Ratufa.distinguishing_notes: Ratufa (giant squirrels) are the largest co-occurring tree squirrels: HB c. 305-460 mm in HMW 2016 species ranges and Moore & Tate type specimens (Ellerman: "usually over 250 mm ... up to 470"); all other genera in this group are <=230 mm except some Callosciurus (HMW max 291 mm for C. inornatus). Dentally Ratufa has only one upper premolar (cheek teeth 4/4, Ellerman 1940 p. 384; P3 absence listed by Moore & Tate 1965 as separating Callosciurus from Ratufa), whereas Callosciurus, Tamiops, Dremomys, Menetes and Funambulus all have P3 (Ellerman 1940; Moore & Tate 1965). Ratufa lacks the light dorsal stripes of Funambulus/Tamiops (Moore & Tate 1965 Funambulus diagnosis). Cheek teeth brachyodont with low cusps and the forefoot with a greatly expanded inner pad (Ellerman 1940). Ear tufts are conspicuous in R. indica, small in R. macroura and gigantea, absent in most R. bicolor (Moore & Tate 1965; HMW 2016) - so ear tufts are not a genus-level separator.

Funambulus.distinguishing_notes: Funambulus (Indian/Sri Lankan palm squirrels) has 3 (or 5 in F. pennantii) PALE longitudinal stripes on a darker back, with a pale mid-dorsal stripe (Moore & Tate 1965 diagnosis char. 5; Ellerman 1940). This separates it from co-occurring Ratufa, Callosciurus and Dremomys (no pale dorsal stripes) and from Tamiops, whose mid-dorsal stripe and its paired stripes are BLACK, with the predominant pale stripes being the outer pair (Moore & Tate 1965 pp. 233-234; Wikipedia/Thorington et al. 2012). Other Moore & Tate characters: baculum a single unit (vs two-part in Callosciurus/Tamiops/Dremomys/Menetes), only two pairs of functional mammae, low, weakly falcate coronoid process. Size (HB 110-195 mm) is far below Ratufa (>=250-305 mm). F. sublineatus/obscurus have reduced, fur-obscured stripes (HMW 2016; Ellerman 1940).

Tamiops.distinguishing_notes: Tamiops: small (HB c. 100-155 mm) striped tree squirrels with a BLACK mid-dorsal stripe flanked by paired dark and pale stripes (5 dark / 4 pale), a pale facial stripe from the rostrum beneath the eye, and small white ear tufts (Moore & Tate 1965; Ellerman 1940; Liu et al. 2022). Vs Funambulus: in Funambulus the mid-stripe and stripes of the same colour are WHITE/pale on a uniformly coloured ground; in Tamiops they are black and the ground between them forms two differently-coloured pairs (Moore & Tate 1965 p. 234). Vs Callosciurus: light dorsal stripes (absent in Callosciurus), orbit <13 mm vs >13 mm, flat rostral profile (Moore & Tate 1965). Vs Dremomys: light dorsal stripes, nasal shorter than interorbital breadth, smaller size (Dremomys >=165 mm). Vs Menetes: Menetes has high-relief cheek teeth with a persistent deep central valley, nasal > interorbital breadth and a markedly elongated rostrum (Moore & Tate 1965; Ellerman 1940); its dark mid-dorsal stripe is variable/absent. Vs Ratufa: size, stripes, P3 present.

Callosciurus.distinguishing_notes: Callosciurus ("beautiful squirrels") are medium tree squirrels (HB c. 148-291 mm, HMW 2016) with extremely variable colouration: many species have a pale and/or dark FLANK stripe (C. notatus, nigrovittatus, adamsi, orestes, baluensis, prevostii, phayrei), others have none (C. caniceps, several C. prevostii subspecies, some C. erythraeus); C. quinquestriatus has black-and-white VENTRAL stripes and an annulated tail; C. finlaysonii ranges from all white to all red to all black. Moore & Tate 1965 genus diagnosis: no pronounced longitudinal stripes on the back (vs Funambulus, Tamiops, Menetes), P3 present (vs Ratufa), least interorbital breadth exceeds nasal length (sole character vs Dremomys), orbit >13 mm (vs Tamiops), baculum of two parts. Caution: a broad black mid-dorsal band occurs in C. erythraeus atrodorsalis/thai, and a pale postauricular patch (otherwise a Dremomys mark) occurs in C. adamsi, C. orestes and some C. nigrovittatus.

Dremomys.distinguishing_notes: Dremomys (plain long-nosed squirrels): drab brown, montane, partly terrestrial squirrels with elongate rostra and short bushy tails (Hawkins et al. 2016), plain dorsum without light stripes (Moore & Tate 1965 char. 7), a small whitish/buffy postauricular patch in all species (Moore & Tate 1965), and in several species red cheeks (rufigenis, ornatus), red throat (gularis), red hip patches (pyrrhomerus) and/or red under-tail/perianal patch (HMW 2016). Vs Callosciurus: nasal length exceeds least interorbital breadth (Moore & Tate's only separating character); shorter tail. Vs Funambulus/Tamiops: no light dorsal stripes. Vs Menetes: no deep dirt-filled valley in the upper cheek teeth, strongly falcate coronoid, no light stripes (Moore & Tate 1965). Vs Ratufa: size, P3 present. Caveats: D. lokriah's rostrum is not longer than in some Callosciurus (Ellerman 1940); a thin black mid-dorsal line occurs in D. pernyi howelli and D. lokriah macmillani; a postauricular patch also occurs in some Callosciurus.

Menetes.distinguishing_notes: Menetes berdmorei (Indochinese ground squirrel): two constant whitish stripes on each side plus 0-3 black lateral lines and sometimes a black mid-dorsal line (Moore & Tate 1965; HMW 2016); markedly elongated rostrum (Ellerman 1940); upper cheek teeth with extraordinarily high relief and a deep, persistent, dirt-filled central valley - Moore & Tate's character (1), which separates Menetes from Ratufa, Funambulus, Callosciurus, Tamiops and Dremomys. Vs Callosciurus: also nasal > interorbital breadth and weakly falcate coronoid; vs Dremomys: light stripes and coronoid; vs Tamiops: larger (HB c. 160-210 vs 100-155 mm), nasal > interorbital, mid-dorsal stripe variable/absent rather than constant black (Ellerman notes that in M. b. decoratus the pattern superficially resembles the chipmunk Tamias, including a black mid-dorsal stripe).
